Patch Set 7: Code-Review+2
Change has been successfully rebased and submitted as 9dffc76cb981f6f2f0a840c857d603832e0919b7
This is going to be problematic when we switch to the AST2700.  What is the alternative to doing devmem operations?

Would it help if we did things like
```
compatible=$(tr -d '\0' < /proc/device-tree/compatible)
if [[ "$compatible" =~ .*ast2600.* ]]; then
   # All AST2600 based devmem hacks
else
   # All AST2700 based devmem hacks
fi
```

Example ast2600
``` 
cat /proc/device-tree/compatible 
facebook,yosemite4-bmcaspeed,ast2600
```

Yes, the 2600 ESPI controller(0x1E6EE000) and 2700 ESPI controller(0x014C05000) is not compatible. 

Intuitive method, refer catalina, but still use devmem.
meta-facebook/meta-catalina/recipes-phosphor/state/phosphor-state-manager/yosemite5/phosphor-state-manager-init
meta-facebook/meta-catalina/recipes-phosphor/state/phosphor-state-manager/yosemite5-2700/phosphor-state-manager-init
Should we use `tr '\0' '\n'` ?
Done
Prefer `aspeed,ast2600` because you could have a machine with a compatible like `facebook,yosemite4-ast2600`.
Done

Honestly, rather than checking at runtime, the better approach is to have a different file snippet installed using the OVERRIDES syntax in Yocto.  There is already an "aspeed-g6" override for the 2600-based platforms and there will be an "aspeed-g7" for the 2700-based platforms.

So the suggestion is have two init files, say phosphor-state-manager-init-ast2600 and phosphor-state-manager-init-ast2700 and in phosphor-state-manager_%.bbappend use
```
SRCURI:aspeed-g6 += "file://phosphor-state-manager-init-ast2600"
SRCURI:aspeed-g7 += "file://phosphor-state-manager-init-ast2700"
```
Yes, but I'd probably do it as `file://ast2700/phosphor-state-manager-init` so that the path in UNPACKDIR is the same for both of them and you don't have to do any funny file renames.
Done
